blocks.text: INNNEWS- When a country starts to have trouble answering criticism with arguments, history shows that power often finds another path: creating enemies. In many regimes, the enemy is usually present in the form of traitors, for foreign officials, for fun and fun agents and foreign agents.
In his report, Amnesty accused the existing digital disformed operation used to discredit activists, journalists, academics and government critics with foreign agent-proofing.
Secretary General Amnesty, Agnes Callayard, has brought very hard accusations on the direction of Indonesian democracy under Prabowo Subianto's government.
In 18 months since the Prabowo ruled, online dissertation appeared as a key tactic to systematically discredit government critics, shutting down public debate, and justifying repression.

According to Amnesty, a number of social media accounts involved in the campaign seem to be affiliated with military elements and political networks associated with the Gerindra Party. Amnesty also states that the narrative of foreign agents is used to delegate civil society groups as well as establish perception that critics against governments are identical to threats against the state.
The writer of Amnesty's report, Chanatip Tatiyakaroonwong, warned that such a label had dangerous social impact.
> Suspend Disinformation is constantly used to label activists, journalists, and human rights defenders as foreign agents can trigger intimidation, threats, even violence.

The statement touched a sensitive point in the history of Indonesian politics. In the time of the New Order, the label against political opposition as a threat to the country was one of the main instruments to limit the critics. Now, according to Amnesty, the pattern is experiencing digital transformations: not through formal sensors alone, but by a massive public opinion operation on social media.

The difference lies in scale and speed. In a digital age, one doesn't need to be locked up for silence. It's pretty corrupted. When an activist is branded a foreign agent, public attention shifts from critical substance to the identity of critic. Critics against economics, democracy, human rights or militarism are no longer rationally disputed, but suspected as an external agenda.

This kind of strategy is effective because it plays on public nationalism psychology. In a society that has long trauma against foreign intervention, the label of foreign agents is easy to trigger emotional anger. Critics are no longer seen as a normal part of democracy, but a threat to the sovereignty of the country.

What makes Amnesty's report even more serious is a wider political context. In the last two years, the Prabowo government expanded military engagement in various civilian sectors. The approach that emphasizes national stability, discipline, and strengthening the security institutions is certainly interesting to some people who are tired of political polarization and economic uncertainty. But history also shows that when stability is made the country's main reason, civil liberties are often the first victims.

Indonesia still has elections today, relatively free media, and active civil society. But modern democracy setbacks rarely occur suddenly. In many cases, democracy is slowly weakened through normalization delegization of critics, the creation of imaginary enemies, and the use of nationalism to attack political opponents.

Therefore, Amnesty's report should not be directly rejected as an alien intervention, but also should not be accepted to affirm. Serious accusations like this require transparent and open answers. If the report is wrong, the government has room to deny it through data, independent investigation, and public clarification. But if this practice is true, then Indonesia is moving towards a new form of digital authoritarianism: electronic democracies are holding elections, but are slowly limiting space dissents through narrative operations and public stigmatization.

In the end, the measure of manhood of democracy is not in the ability of the country to create enemies, but in the courage of the state to receive criticism without having to label its critics as a nation's threat.
